column1: # Canada outside Toronto, Montreal and Ottawa (ca.cautious): no majority. Members, each with its own summer rule
# fitted on its tables: the Edmonton mosques' 18° family (ca.eighteen: Al Omari, Al Ansar, Al Farooq; Surrey Jamea in
# BC, 18°/17°, one month), Edmonton's 15° family (ca.fifteen: Markaz Al Imam Malik) and Calgary Islamic Centre SW's 15°
# with Isha = Maghrib + 90 (ca.isha90). Each table is its own mosque's (the research's index: slug, city, point); none
# prints an imsak, so each Fajr is also the start of the fast. Maghrib is checked like every start at every table, Calgary
# Islamic Centre SW's and Imam Malik's too, whose Maghribs are within minutes of sunset: the 18° family's (Maghrib + 5 to 6
# at Al Omari), the latest, is shown (ruling R155; until then the 26 Sep cap followed it and left those two unchecked).
# Faults left out in the Task 7g copies under
# namerica/split-7g/ (proof.md). Not members (proof.md): IISC Calgary (10°/10°), Al-Medina and Assiddiq Edmonton,
# Al-Rahmah Surrey (18°/15° Hanafi, one month), Burnaby's 2015 table and Eyup Sultan (Diyanet). Every row is held out.
# `clock`: Calgary Islamic Centre SW, Al Omari, Al Ansar and Al Farooq print their 2026 tables on Alberta's old clock, back
# to UTC-7 on 1 November. Alberta keeps UTC-6 all year from that day (tz 2026c), so America/Edmonton reads those Novembers
# and Decembers an hour off on a new tz database and right on an old one. Their rows are read on America/Denver, which keeps
# Alberta's old clock exactly (America/Edmonton before 2026c, every day of 2026 and 2027), on any tz database. Markaz Al Imam
# Malik prints the new clock (no going back); its copy's days end on 31 October (its @excuse below), so it needs none.
# Ruling R117: the faults the Task 7g copies leave out, named in their headers (proof.md), as the gate reads them
# (@excuse: entry, member, the table's lat,lon, the dates, fault, the reason).
